title: "Shell and Editor Configuration"

# Shell and Editor Configuration

Setting up Zsh, Fish, Bash, and editors on new machines usually requires copying snippets and installing plugins by hand. The boring default is: **declare shell aliases, plugins, prompts, and editor settings natively in Home Manager**.

## Mental model

Home Manager provides high-level modules for major tools:
- `programs.zsh`: Configures completions, history size, and plugins.
- `programs.starship`: Cross-shell prompt configured declaratively.
- `programs.git`: Declares name, email, signing keys, and global ignore lists.

## Worked examples

Save as `shell_editor.nix`:

```nix
# shell_editor.nix
{
  programs.git = {
    enable = true;
    userName = "Desk Engineer";
    userEmail = "desk@corp.internal";
    extraConfig = {
      init.defaultBranch = "main";
      pull.rebase = true;
    };
  };

  programs.starship = {
    enable = true;
    settings = {
      add_newline = false;
      format = "$directory$character";
    };
  };
}
```

## The boring rule

- Configure Git, shell, and prompts through typed `programs.*` options.
- Avoid manual plugin managers; let Nix fetch and lock shell plugins.
